VERDICT: proceed with these caveats: no source supplied — fidelity and omission unchecked; the replay that scores the fix (FIX-002) was run on the first wording of the clause, not the shipped one, so the shipped prompt is unscored; the allow case passes with or without the fix, so nothing shows the live block is fixed (it never reproduced); nothing automated asserts the clause stays in the built prompt and settings files

Coverage: 5 of 5 verifiers reported. 7 requirements and 2 tasks indexed. No PRD exists for this defect, so validation against product requirements was NOT checked. Only traceability between the TRD and the delivered code was checked.

TRACEABILITY GAPS — implemented, no test proving it
- The shipped wording of the clause was never replayed (FIX-002-AC). The replay ran at 16:57 on "a running task the agent did not start ... keeps no promise either". The end-of-run review commit 5d67c7b5 (17:02) then narrowed it to "armed on its own ... keeps none for other work". replay-after.jsonl quotes the old text 4 times and the new text 0 times. Covered by FIX-002, so this chains to /implement-trd --reconcile, which re-runs score.py on the current built prompt.
- The promise-block objective (O2) is proven only by that stale replay (5/5 blocked on both block cases). No Jest, BATS or pytest test asserts it. Covered by FIX-002, so this chains to /implement-trd --reconcile.

UNTESTED-IN-PRACTICE — a test exists but does not prove the requirement
- The allow objective (O1), and the allow case inside FIX-002: the replay case stands for the reported block, but it already passed with the pre-change prompt (0 of 5 runs blocked, 0 of 20 across variants). Passing it shows no regression. It does not show the clause causes the allow. The TRD discloses this, and the owner has to decide whether that is enough evidence (confirm-wanted). A real case needs the live transcript or the block reason from the owner's session.
- The clause has no regression guard (FIX-001). I re-checked by hand: 'armed on its own' appears once in the built prompt, the vendored prompt, all three settings.json files and docs/reference/hooks.md. The vendored copy is byte-identical to the built one, and `npx jest packages/core/hooks/prompts` passes 32 of 32. But no test would catch the clause being dropped later. Nothing is defective today.

REJECTED THESE FINDINGS
- none. I re-checked every finding against the files and all of them hold.

NO ACTION — implemented, tested, sourced
- FIX-001's acceptance criteria are met as written. Verified in packages/core/hooks/prompts/discipline-stop.prompt.md (4,880 bytes, under the 6,000-character limit) and .claude/hooks/prompts/discipline-stop.prompt.md. The matching exemption is in .claude/rules/async-discipline.md:45.

Could Not Verify, rewritten in /private/tmp/ensemble-vnext-feature-6-fix-stop-judge-auto-armed-monitor/docs/TRD/stop-judge-auto-armed-monitor.md: 4 entries. They are: no PRD, so validation is unchecked; the live block is unreproduced and its transcript sits under the owner's account; the allow case's final message was written for the TRD, not taken from the real turn; the watch's entry shape in `background_tasks` is assumed (open question OQ-1). The stale-replay gap is not listed there because it is an audit finding, reported above.

requirements.statement: The Stop judge (discipline-stop) allows a finished turn whose only running background task is the live-updates watch the platform arms itself when an artifact is published. Must pass.
The judge still blocks a turn that promises later work nothing will keep, whether background_tasks is empty or holds only that auto-armed watch. Must pass.

A running task the platform armed on its own is neither evidence of a promise nor something that keeps one. A finished turn with only that task running is allowed; a promise of other work is judged exactly as if the task were absent.
The change is one added clause in the existing 'Not case A' paragraph of discipline-stop.source.md, not a new paragraph, with the exact wording given in Decision.

The built prompt and all three settings.json contain the clause; the vendored prompt is byte-identical to the built one; npx jest packages/core/hooks/prompts passes (prompt under 6,000 characters, one $ARGUMENTS).
requirements.source: TRD Master Task List, FIX-001 Acceptance Criteria

requirements.statement: Replay on claude-sonnet-5, 5 runs each, gives: aam-complete-monitor-only-allow allowed 5/5; aam-own-monitor-plus-auto-allow allowed in at least 4/5; aam-promise-no-tasks-block and aam-promise-monitor-only-block each blocked in at least 4/5; the four s-payload-escape-* cases keep their pre-change majority verdict; no run errors.
requirements.source: TRD Master Task List, FIX-002 Acceptance Criteria

requirements.statement: No change to case B, the loop guard, the output format, or the replay harness (score.py, report.py). The prompt stays under the 6,000-character limit.

tasks.description: Add the auto-armed-task clause to the 'Not case A' paragraph of discipline-stop.source.md; rebuild with build-judge-prompts.js then generate-hooks-artifacts.sh; copy the built prompt to .claude/hooks/prompts/discipline-stop.prompt.md; add the clause to rule 3 of the decision table in docs/reference/hooks.md section 6.2. Dependencies: none. Serves O1, O2.

Keep the replay cases in test/discipline-corpus/replay/cases/auto-armed-monitor-2026-11-20.jsonl (four new, four copied from the 2026-09-23 fixture) and score the new built prompt on them, 5 runs each, on claude-sonnet-5. Dependencies: FIX-001. Serves O1, O2.

could_not_verify: The live block did not reproduce in replay. The current prompt already allows the reconstructed allow case (0 of 5 runs blocked, and 0 of 20 across five variants), so the allow criterion in FIX-002 would pass without the fix. Passing it shows the new paragraph causes no regression; it does not show the live case is fixed. That needs the 2026-11-20 live transcript (owner's account, not readable from this one), extracted with test/discipline-corpus/replay/extract.py, or a new live occurrence.

The final message of the allow case is a /plan readout written for this TRD, not the blocked turn's real text. Owner: the block reason shown as 'Stop hook error: ...' in that session, or its transcript, would turn this into a real case.
The shape of the auto-armed watch in background_tasks is assumed (OQ-1).
open_questions: OQ-1: What exact background_tasks entry does the auto-armed watch produce? Assumed: {id, type: "monitor", status: "running", description: "Live updates: <artifact url>"}; the prompt names the watch by what it is, not by field values. Owner-only: no.
